## What I built

The request — "bring back a client I tucked away" — is a **restore (un-archive)** feature. The `archived` column already existed (V19), so no new migration was needed; I added the missing behaviour across the stack, all additively per the app's conventions:

**Server (OfficeFloor + Spring)**
- `ClientsRestore.java` + `RestoreClient.java` + `rest/api/clients/restore.POST.yml` — `POST /api/clients/restore` clears the archived flag (the inverse of `ClientsArchive`) and records `CLIENT_RESTORED id=<id>` through the `Audit` service.
- `ClientsArchivedGet.java` + `rest/api/clients/archived.GET.yml` + a `findByArchivedTrueOrderByIdAsc()` repository method — `GET /api/clients/archived` surfaces the tucked-away clients. The default `GET /api/clients` stays non-archived-only, so other consumers (the project form's client select, search) are untouched.
- `TestSupportController` — the client seed now honours the fixture's `archived` flag (it previously inserted only `id, name, email`, so the spec's archived `Old Client` would have seeded un-archived).

**Front-end (all new files, nothing edited)**
- `features/clients/showArchived.slot.tsx` — a `clients-show-archived` toggle filling the clients toolbar, owning the `showArchived` URL search param.
- `features/clients/archived.slot.tsx` — a toolbar panel that reads the same `showArchived` key and, when on, lists archived clients each with a `client-restore-<id>` button. Restore is a `useMutation` that invalidates `['clients']`, so the client drops out of the panel and reappears in the default table with nothing hand-maintained.

The two features coordinate only through the shared `showArchived` URL key and the `['clients']` query key — no imports, no callbacks, no page edits.
